title: Staged fallback and capacity replenishment protocol
content:
Purpose:
This document is a working draft runbook for handling multi-node GPU infra degradations where we need to: 1) isolate unhealthy nodes, 2) keep customer traffic healthy via staged fallbacks, 3) inject temporary capacity, and 4) perform safe GPU replacement or node recovery. It complements other SRE playbooks by focusing on coordinated capacity replenishment and progressive degradation rather than full cluster evacuation.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated clusters running the inference serving runtime (K8s-backed).
- Assumes on-call has access to the SRE runbook Slack channel (#sre-ops), infra console, and the on-call admin key vault.
- This is NOT the hardware replacement spec; it focuses on immediate traffic and capacity controls until replacement/maintenance completes.

When to use this protocol (trigger conditions):
- Persistent GPU hardware errors (ECC, thermal throttling, persistent CUDA faults) on >= 2 nodes in a AZ, or a single node causing >10% token lat SLO breach for 15+ minutes.
- Autoscaler failing to bring replacement nodes within configured warmup time.
- Degraded model throughput where short-term capacity injection would avoid customer impact.

High-level goals (in order):
1) Prevent cascade: remove affected nodes from scheduling and stop new stateful work on them.
2) Maintain latency SLOs: route critical traffic to healthy pools or cheaper-latency fallbacks.
3) Maintain correctness: ensure model replica consistency when moving traffic between quantized and non-quantized variants.
4) Restore capacity: inject ephemeral nodes or burst pool while hardware repairs progress.
5) Prepare for post-incident analysis: capture logs, traces, and decisions.

Immediate checklist for on-call (first 10 minutes):
- Acknowledge alert and create incident in PagerDuty/JIRA (tag SRE-INC).
- Post an initial incident summary in #sre-ops: cause (if known), scope, immediate mitigation, ETA for updates.
- Run quick health queries:
  - kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep -E "NotReady|gpu-fault"
  - kubectl describe node <node> (check kubelet errors, OOMs, taints)
  - /ops/infra/metrics query: token_p50_latency, token_error_rate, gpu_ecc_errors (last 1h)
- Add node(s) to a temporary taint list so autoschedulers and batch jobs won't place new pods: kubectl taint nodes <node> redwood/sre=isolated:NoSchedule --overwrite
- If node shows memory/GPU driver crashloop, cordon & drain non-critical pods: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60

Staged fallback routing (if latency SLO is in jeopardy):
- Identify critical routes (from alert metadata / console) and move to faster paths: e.g., route internal-hosted customers to dedicated fast-pool or lower-cost fallback model variant.
- Use Console route policy UI or API: set route override to model-variant: "fast-32k" with traffic=10% canary, then 100% if stable.
- If fallback requires changing model precision (FP16->INT8), run quick smoke tests against the evaluation prompt set for the route to ensure quality delta is acceptable. Document test ID and result.

Short-term capacity injection (when injection is allowed):
- Preconditions: approvals from SRE lead or on-call escalation, capacity budget check, confirmation that autoscaler cannot recover in 10–20m.
- Procedure:
  1) Provision ephemeral GPU instances from the burst pool (runbook script): /ops/scripts/provision-ephemeral.sh --count=<n> --instance-type=A100-40GB --tag=ephemeral-surge-<incident-id>
  2) Add nodes to k8s cluster: /ops/scripts/join-node.sh <node-ip>
  3) Verify GPU driver and runtime health: nvidia-smi; /ops/scripts/gpu-smoke.sh <node-ip>
  4) Remove ignition taints so schedulers can place pods: kubectl label node <node> ephemeral=surge; kubectl untaint nodes <node> redwood/sre=isolated:NoSchedule
  5) Observe scheduling and warmup: watch pod startup logs, check model coldstart latency for 5–10 minutes.
- If provisioning fails or new nodes crash, rollback by deprovisioning ephemeral nodes and escalate to infra eng.

Safe node replacement and GPU swap (coordinated with hardware/field ops):
- Do not proceed until hardware ticket exists and assigned.
- When field ops are ready, cordon the node if not already cordoned. Ensure all inference pods are drained or rescheduled.
- Capture final diagnostics: /ops/diagnostics/gpu-dump.sh <node> -> upload to incident artifacts.
- Accept that traffic will be shifted away for the maintenance window; set console route fallback to stable variant during swap window.

Validation and roll-forward criteria:
- P50 latency returns to < SLO threshold for 10 consecutive minutes across impacted routes.
- Error rate (model errors + 5xx) drops below baseline + 2 sigma.
- All ephemeral nodes show stable GPU utilization and no ECC/driver errors for 30 minutes.
- If criteria met, scale down burst pool by 20% every 10 minutes until normal autoscaler resumes.

Rollback and emergency stop:
- If fallback causes data-quality regressions or unacceptable hallucination increases, abort and roll traffic back to previous variant. Record reasoning in incident log.
- If ephemeral nodes introduce instability (kernel oops or OOMs), immediately cordon and deprovision them.

Monitoring & telemetry to capture during incident:
- GPU ECC errors, temperature, power draw (nvidia-smi export).
- Token-level p50/p95/p99 latencies per route and per model variant.
- Pod restart counts and kubelet logs for drained nodes.
- Console traces for cold-start sequences.
- Snapshot of autoscaler decisions and cluster utilization.

Escalation matrix (if recovery stalls > 30m):
- SRE on-call -> SRE lead (paging) -> Infrastructure engineering -> Field hardware ops.
- For customer-impacting SLO breaches notify customer-success: cs-ops@redwood.ai and create a CS incident link.

Post-incident: immediate 48-hour actions:
- Collate logs, GPU dumps, and ephemeral node metadata into incident JIRA ticket.
- Create short postmortem summary (1 page) and paste into confluence link in linked_artifacts. Include timeline, decisions, metrics before/after.
- Open follow-up tasks: kernel/driver upgrade, autoscaler tuning, burst-pool capacity targets. Assign owners and ETA.

Suggested improvements (to be discussed in retro):
- Automate smoke-evals against fallback model variants so canary decisions are faster.
- Introduce automated ephemeral provisioning with circuit-breaker that limits burst when driver errors are present.
- Add a synthetic probe that detects pre-failure GPU symptoms (temperature trend + ECC) and pre-warms spare capacity.

Incident notes template (to paste into JIRA during the incident):
- Summary: short statement of problem and immediate mitigation.
- Impacted routes: list.
- Timeline: hh:mm action by (ack, cordon, provision, route-change, verify).
- Decisions: what fallback chosen and why.
- Next steps: short list with owners.

Open questions and TODOs for this draft:
- What is the exact cost-accounting process for ephemeral bursts across customer tenants? (finance input needed)
- Should fallbacks to INT8 variants be blocked automatically for customers with strict quality SLAs?
- Define a permanent telemetry dashboard for GPU pre-failure indicators.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is purposely conservative about switching model variants; the eval step exists because quality regressions are a real customer risk.
- Look for missing edge-cases (cross-AZ failovers, multi-tenant burst budget conflicts).

End of draft.
